We practiced short rebuttals, demo handoffs, and agreed owner tasks to create short video snippets and update the objection playbook.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-08-04 10:00 PDT | Duration 75m | Location: Zoom | Recording: yes
Attendees: Avery Chen (AE), Marco Alvarez (SE), Janelle Park (Head of SE), Tom Reed (Solutions Eng), Priya Nambiar (Prod-Marketing), Evan Soto (Enablement)

00:00 Avery: okay team, we got 75 minutes, tight agenda. main goals, run the five minute elevator demo, spar on objections and rehearse two technical deep dive snippets. keep it messy—this is sparring.
00:18 Marco: yeah and I want to stress the KV cache demo — people get lost when we say "cache" and then jump to quantization, they glaze over. we need micro clips like 60 seconds that show before/after token latency.
00:32 Janelle: totally. also we keep hitting the same security questions — "how do you handle keys, KMS, HSM" — we need a 30-second crisp answer that isn't legalese.
00:47 Tom: one more, when customers ask about private vs hosted, the common misbelief is that hosted equals data copying offsite. we need a two-sentence policy explanation and when to push Dedicated vs Private.
01:03 Avery: ok first up, 5-min elevator demo. Marco you'll run it, I will shadow for handoffs. Marco you start with prompt engineering, then show streaming and cost dashboard. good?
01:12 Marco: yep. starting now. "Hey I'm Marco from Redwood, we're a platform for predictable LLM inference..." (demo running) okay streaming comes in here, note the tokens per second. um, latency at 1.2 sec for a 120-token response — cold start, notice KV cache off.
03:40 Priya: small nit — when you say "predictable" can we replace with "predictable latency and cost"? it's more concrete.
03:50 Marco: good call. I say predictable latency and cost.
04:05 Evan: objection practice: customer says "we already use OpenAI, why Redwood?" Marco?
04:12 Marco: traditional answer: you can use modern models with better cost control, but we need a concrete differentiator — e.g., unified routing and fallbacks, dedicated pools for SLOs.
04:28 Janelle: add a line about rollout control — canary, A/B, automatic fallback to cheaper model during overload. customers like operational stories.
04:44 Tom: roleplay time. I'm the security director: "How do you handle KMS and audit logs?"
04:51 Marco (as seller): we support customer managed KMS and HSM integrations, full audit logs with per-request metadata, and SSO/SAML for admin access.
05:05 Tom (as sec dir): ok layer two follow-up: "where are logs stored, and can we purge them on-demand?"
05:12 Marco: we have retention policies and export/purge APIs, and for Private deployments logs remain in your VPC per the config.
05:27 Tom: slight hesitation — transcript shows he said "V P C" once as "VPC" but often the wording in the pitch gets fuzzy, make that crisp: "logs remain in your VPC and you control retention via API".
05:45 Avery: good. now advanced objection: "Your costs look lower, but we have unpredictable bursty traffic — how do we avoid SLA misses?"
05:54 Marco: reply: reserved capacity (Dedicated) plus burst pool is the right answer; emphasize autoscale config and fallback to compatible smaller model variants.
06:12 Janelle: bring in an anecdote — last quarter we had customer X who used canary with fallback and avoided 30% latency spike. numbers sell.
06:28 Marco: ok I'll add a quick metric: "we saw <2% error rate during a 10x burst after implementing fallback" — need to confirm precise numbers later.
06:38 Priya: note — do not invent exact metrics in live calls. phrase as "in one case" unless we have a public benchmark link.
06:47 Marco: noted.
07:01 Avery: demo practice number two: show hosted vs dedicated routing in console. Marco?
07:08 Marco: launching console. screen share hiccup... (brief pause) — ok I have the routes page. here you can pin model version and select dedicated pool, or choose hosted with routing policy.
07:35 Tom: small ui callout: highlight the route priority and fallback toggles — customers miss that in slide decks.
07:44 Marco: done. I toggled fallback to smaller-quantized model as an example. latency changes from 1.2s to 1.8s but cost drops 40% — rough numbers.
08:10 Janelle: practice the handoff: AE should ask if they care about percentiles, not averages. correct phrasing: "Are you working to a p95 or p99 SLO or is average latency sufficient?"
08:25 Avery: nifty. next exercise: two-minute KV-cache demo. Marco you'll show prefix caching for a chat app.
08:33 Marco: demo start: initial prompt, then same conversation repeated with prefix cached, watch first token latency drop from 180ms to 40ms.
09:12 Priya: great visual. again, label it "prefix/KV cache" and don't call it "memory" — customers confuse with stateful storage.
09:22 Marco: ack.
09:27 Evan: practice the pricing objection: "If you add caching, does that increase our storage costs?"
09:33 Marco: answer: minimal — caching is ephemeral and typically reduces overall token spend; explain cost amortization per request.
09:44 Tom: interject technical deep-dive for SEs: some prospects will ask about kernel selection and quantization. keep one line: "we auto-select kernels based on model arch and sequence length; quantized paths reduce memory and cost with small quality tradeoff".
10:02 Janelle: roleplay a hard procurement question: "We need SOC 2, ISO, and contractual audits — can you support?"
10:09 Marco: yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO roadmaps, plus audit logs. for Private deployments we can meet more stringent audits.
10:19 Avery: low confidence note, Marco — say "we have SOC 2 Type II and ongoing ISO 27001 efforts". don't promise ISO unless legal sign-off.
10:29 Marco: fixed.
10:35 Priya: quick competitive framing exercise. how to respond when buyer says "Why not run huggingface on our own infra?"
10:42 Tom: answer: you can self-host, but you trade off the ops burden — we provide runtime optimizations, continuous kernel selection, and smart routing that most infra teams find expensive to build. point them to case studies.
10:58 Marco: objection: "What about models like Claude that we already use?" reply: we support multi-model routing and can orchestrate Claude alongside open models; emphasize unified governance and cost controls.
11:12 Janelle: important to coach SEs to ask clarifying questions before defending — often the buyer is fishing for price, not product.
11:25 Avery: roleplay: I'm an engineer asking about cold-starts and batch sizes. go.
11:31 Marco (as SE): our runtime uses continuous batching and warm pools, plus prefix cache to reduce cold-start impact. cold-start across GPUs varies but we keep it bounded with warm pools.
11:54 Tom: cross talk: mention that kernel selection can change latency curve — but again keep it high level.
12:05 Priya: content ask — can someone make two short videos: 1) KV cache before/after, 2) hosted vs dedicated routing toggle? marketing needs them for playbooks.
12:15 Marco: I can do the KV cache clip.
12:18 Avery: Priya will produce the hosted vs dedicated clip. Evan will stitch and annotate.
12:25 Evan: timeline?
12:27 Priya: end of next week? 2025-08-08?
12:32 Marco: yes that's doable.
12:36 Avery: ok final section — demo timing and handoffs. AE should own intro and qualifying, SE takes demo from slide 3 onward, AE returns for business questions and pricing. practice that handoff once. Marco take it.
12:48 Marco: handoff happening... (demo run) and handing back to Avery.
13:20 Avery: landing question: "Do you need a POC or a quick pilot to validate latency and cost?" keep script: "We recommend a 2-4 week pilot with a small traffic-sample to validate SLOs and cost."
13:34 Janelle: include acceptance criteria: p95 under X ms, cost per 1k tokens under Y (tailor per prospect).
13:45 Tom: note to SEs: ask for logs access and sample prompt set as part of pilot. that's how we measure regressions.
13:59 Avery: closing recap — we agreed on demo edits, two video snippets, and updated playbook. any other items?
14:06 Priya: I'll add competitor notes.
14:11 Marco: I'll record the clips.
14:15 Janelle: I'll run the SDR practice session next week.
14:20 Avery: perfect. end meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: multiple short gaps due to screen-sharing and demo audio; a few technical terms mis-transcribed (e.g., "KV cache" written as "K V cache" in places; "HSM" once transcribed as "H S M").

Artifacts referenced: link:internal/playbooks/se-objection-playbook (internal link), link:internal/videos/kv-cache-demo (placeholder), link:internal/videos/hosted-vs-dedicated (placeholder), link:internal/security/security-whitepaper.pdf

Recap (AE): Avery to circulate cleaned 5-minute demo script and updated slide deck. Marco to record two demo snippets. Janelle to schedule SDR practice. Priya/Evan to produce the annotated videos.

End of transcript.
